analysis:
The only changed file is CHANGELOG.md, a documentation file that renders v0.10.7 candidate release notes (base lines 11-13 replaced by head lines 11-413). There is no executable code, config or protocol change in this diff, so no security control is directly altered. The base unit is far-back historical text (lines 3861+); the head unit is the new top section (lines 1-227 visible). No regression identified.

Content relevant to threat entries, described as shipped behavior in the notes and not verified against source here: (1) App Attest restart/recovery and the new app-attest-verified.json state file (lines 27-37) touch A-015/A-016/TB-011; the notes say the provider fills it from daemon-state.json using evidence from the last 7 days. Whether this restores or extends any authorization lifetime is a code question (T-053/T-057). It is described as only a restart trigger, with the coordinator remaining the grantor, which is consistent with the stated model. (2) The cluster self-update path (lines 59-68, 99-105) downloads, verifies and stages releases, rolls back to the prior release, and quarantines the new one, which touches T-043 (rollback authority is the same replaceable binary) and update integrity. A rollback to the earlier kept release (`darkbloom update --rollback`, lines 20, 99-105) could downgrade a pair to a release that was later revoked; the notes do not say whether revocation or qualification is rechecked on rollback (T-054). (3) Cache checkpoint encode/decode optimizations (lines 39-57) touch T-041; the notes claim the same bytes and the same refusals, so the at-rest format, HMAC names, TTL and AAD are unchanged. (4) The Gemma 4 tensor-parallel SSD and prompt prefix cache (line 176) is a new encrypted-link feature that relies on the T-041 posture. (5) Two-Mac cluster pairing, new public models and coordinator registration affect the TB-002 and TB-011 trust model; this is source-level work outside the supplied evidence. The note that mismatched builds refuse to pair is fail-closed.

These are descriptive claims only. Code-level review of the referenced PRs (#1702, #1729, #1739, #1706, #1707, #1715) is needed to confirm them.
